claims: Artemis II is the first crewed flight test of NASA's Orion spacecraft and Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Artemis II is designed to validate life-support systems, navigation, and deep-space performance with four astronauts.
Artemis II is scheduled for April 2026.
Artemis II is a 10-day mission.
Artemis II will perform a lunar flyby.
Artemis II is a precursor to future lunar landings (Artemis III/IV).
Artemis II is a precursor to sustained lunar exploration.
Artemis II will test Orion's life support systems with a crew on board.
Artemis II will test Orion's communications systems with a crew on board.
Artemis II will test Orion's navigation systems with a crew on board.
Artemis II will move beyond Earth's magnetic field and radiation protection.
Artemis II will evaluate human health impacts.
Artemis II will evaluate spacecraft performance.
Artemis II will take humans farther than ever before.
Artemis II will perform manual maneuvering of the Orion capsule in close proximity to the ICPS (Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage).
Artemis II's manual maneuvering of the Orion capsule simulates future docking with lunar landers.
Artemis II aims to establish a sustained presence on the Moon as a stepping stone to eventually sending humans to Mars.
Artemis II will gather data on radiation.
Artemis II will gather data on microgravity.
Artemis II includes the AVATAR (A Virtual Astronaut Tissue Analog Response) investigation.
The AVATAR investigation is on the impact of radiation on human health.
The crew of Artemis II includes NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch.
The crew of Artemis II includes Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
